doc.title: Don Alias interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 6, 2002

chapter: Jaco, Weather Report and pop work
title: Jaco's sound, the Osaka river, and Kenny Kirkland
summary: He credits Jaco's sound to the player and his Acoustic amp, recalls the bass in the Osaka river and Donna Lee with congas, and mentions Kenny Kirkland.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: What was it about his sound? I mean aside from all the beautiful technical, amazing technical stuff he did it was like one note, he had this particular sound. Was there equipment behind that? Was there something about his bass or was it just him?

You say was it just him? Was it his bass? I’ve got to say it’s a combination of all of those. I remember in Osaka in Japan and Jaco threw his bass into the Osaka River. Them Japanese guys jumped in and got it. And Jaco thought that that was — he thought that that was a great act. He was like “oh man this cat jumped in the river and got my bass.” And he thought that that was just like a spiritual thing. And he had that acoustic amp that he always used you know, and I suppose that had a great deal to do with the sound. That’s the only piece of equipment that I ever saw him play was that Acoustic thing. And a combination of him and that made his sound. Incredible. I mean I didn’t realize the impact that he would have on the music. Because we were just like kids playing in a pen or something you know. We were just like kids running around playing basketball and doing things. But then he’d sit down and play “Donna Lee” on the bass with conga drums. Brilliant, brilliant idea.
Well thanks for sharing that. Really, I know you were pretty close to him.

Yeah. It was hard. Him and Kenny Kirkland. I gave Kenny his first gig coming out of school, we played with Miroslav together. Another sweet person and a great musician. Those two guys really got inside me.
